problem: Drivers are not warned in real-time when their calculated route polyline intersects high precipitation radar polygons during monsoon seasons.
root_cause: Lack of geospatial intersection checking between active navigation route polylines and real-time precipitation radar polygon feeds/layers.
architecture: Geospatial service daemon layer that periodically fetches radar polygon hazards, matches them against active route polylines using spatial intersection algorithms, and triggers real-time UI/push warnings.
recommended_solution: Implement a spatial intersection module in the backend orchestrator using Turf.js or Python shapely to evaluate route polylines against high-precipitation polygons, and emit real-time hazard alerts to the client app.
risks: High latency from frequent polygon-polyline spatial queries.
False positive hazard alerts due to outdated radar polygon feeds.
acceptance_criteria: System successfully detects intersections between a route polyline and high precipitation radar polygons.
Real-time alerts are pushed to the driver when a hazard intersection is identified.
Performance remains within acceptable limits (<200ms check time).
